To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a crystal as a replacement for a magnet is a new technique for charged particle beam transport and that the crystal septum is a practical tool to increase the maximum momentum that can be transmitted to an experiment.

a bent silicon crystal was successfully used to replace a magnetic septum, that the crystal was able to transmit a beam with 400 GeV/c momentum and 2 x 1011 particles per pulse, and that the crystal was not damaged during the experiment.

the crystal channeling method has been used to increase the momentum range of particles transmitted to an experimental station from the septum limit of about 225 GeV / c to the full momentum of the primary beam of 400 GeVs/c.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a bent crystal as a particle separator and as a replacement for a magnet in a particle beam.
the use of bent crystals to deflect charged particles in a beam, with the ultimate objective of replacing magnets in a charged particle transport system.
the development of crystal-based devices to manipulate the properties of charged particle beams, including the ability to deflect and focus particles.

the crystal magnet replacement experiment at Fermilab was a success.
a bent crystal can replace a magnet to bend a charged particle beam.
the crystal septum has been demonstrated to be an effective replacement for a conventional magnetic septum.

we have demonstrated a new technique that can be applied to a broad spectrum of particle accelerators and storage rings.
a crystal septum can replace a magnetic device in a particle beam.
the bent crystal septum is a viable replacement for a conventional magnetic septum in charged particle beams.
